reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a studio-style discussion of Bitcoin ETFs, futures support, and a possible Goldman Sachs cryptocurrency platform as qualified financial news rather than a direct offer to viewers. The listed donations and Coinbase referral benefit are not connected to guaranteed returns, required investment participation, or deceptive outcomes.

opening.argument: Judge, the description does more than offer market commentary: it promises a cash benefit for taking a specific action. It says, “Sign up and buy on Coinbase to receive $10 for Free!” and supplies a signup link. That is a direct reward-and-purchase solicitation placed alongside a video about growing access to Bitcoin trading. The reward may be modest, but its role is concrete: it gives viewers a reason to move from listening to buying through the provided link.

citations.quote: Sign up and buy on Coinbase to receive $10 for Free! https://www.coinbase.com/join/529b4566229f2d548e000092
they will be supporting CBOE Bitcoin futures for their clients!

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense cites the discussion of exchange filings and trading-platform support, but news content does not erase the separate solicitation in the description. Nor does the absence of guaranteed investment returns answer the narrower concern: the stated $10 reward is conditioned on signing up and buying. A judge should assess that action-linked offer, not only the spoken news segment.

citations.quote: Sign up and buy on Coinbase to receive $10 for Free!
has apparently filed this week with the SEC

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The description does contain a Coinbase signup incentive, but the cited words openly state the condition: sign up and buy to receive $10. They do not show a false reward, a guaranteed investment return, or a deceptive claim about what happens after purchase. The spoken discussion also distinguishes proposals from completed launches, saying there is no official date for the ETFs. A disclosed referral benefit beside qualified financial news is not, by itself, evidence of a scam.

opening.argument: Judge, consider the signals together. The description invites viewers interested in “creative ways to acquire passive income,” then advertises a discount code for a Genesis Mining contract and says using it brings an instant 3% rebate. A mining contract is the purchase pathway; the passive-income framing supplies the appeal. The same description provides cryptocurrency donation addresses. None of those elements proves a loss occurred, but together they make the video more than detached reporting: it directs an income-seeking audience toward a discounted paid mining product.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense is right that the spoken Goldman Sachs report is qualified; that does not address the mining-contract promotion in the description. Its point that no guaranteed return is promised is narrower than the concern here. The channel introduces itself through passive-income content and gives viewers a code to obtain a discounted mining contract. The news segment supplies context, while the description supplies a purchase path.

citations.quote: if this does happen
creative ways to acquire passive income
Receive 3% off of your Genesis Mining Contract Instantly!

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The opening connects two separate statements more tightly than the evidence permits. “Passive income” describes the channel's general subject matter; the Genesis Mining passage promises a discount on a contract, not recurring mining income or a particular return. Cryptocurrency donation addresses likewise request support for the channel, not investment. Those disclosures warrant scrutiny, but they do not establish a deceptive paid-mining returns offer in this video.

opening.argument: Judge, the news format also functions as a path toward participation. The speaker calls a possible ETF approval “a very big day for crypto currencies” and urges listeners to appreciate the significance of ETrade's futures support. The description then offers a concrete next step: sign up and buy on Coinbase for $10. Read together, the favorable institutional narrative builds confidence while the linked offer converts that interest into a purchase. The invitation is in the video's own description, not an unrelated offer imagined by the viewer.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the spoken reporting and the description as separate, but a viewer receives both with the video. Qualifying the Goldman Sachs rumor does not remove the affirmative framing around ETFs and ETrade, or the Coinbase purchase incentive below it. The issue is not whether the speaker guarantees returns; it is whether ostensibly informational coverage steers viewers toward a rewarded signup and purchase.

citations.quote: I personally think it's only a matter of time before every financial institution kind of jumps on board as well.
Sign up and buy on Coinbase to receive $10 for Free!

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Optimistic commentary and a referral link can coexist with financial news without making the reporting deceptive. The speaker explicitly says ETF approval has no official date and describes the Goldman Sachs report as partly rumor. The Coinbase line offers a stated signup benefit; it does not claim that buying will profit, that the reported developments have already happened, or that viewers must act before an opportunity disappears.
